definition: Self-organization here means emergence of pattern through component interactions. The toy couple operation copies one cell’s Boolean state to its neighbor, leaving the first unchanged; it is a local alignment rule with a stable output. It contains neither a reproduction operation nor a goal representation nor an intelligent agent. Dye’s mechanical feedback couples polarity to cell rearrangements; the toy is not a formalization of that continuum theory or of all positive/negative feedback.
note: Stipulated smallest finite demonstration of alignment and stability; the primary experiment is preserved as its own source claim, without claiming the toy reproduces it.
